title: I built an iOS backgammon app with AI - why a simple, evergreen game could be a great place to start
author: AffectionateBag8448
selftext:
Like a lot of you, I tried building several games with AI and kept getting stuck. It couldn't hold my artistic vision, and it was inconsistent with character and world building. I'd sink hours into a creative idea and end up with something I knew wasn't sustainable or going to find an audience.

I don't think that's permanent. AI will get there, or my skills with the current models will. But for now I went back to the drawing board and looked for something that didn't need much artistic design to work and that people would still have a lot of fun playing.

I spend a lot of my free time on chess apps, and I grew up playing backgammon with my family. Every backgammon app I downloaded was outdated, buggy, or shoving coin purchases down my throat. Artistically, all I needed was a board that looked decent - which still took me longer than I expected. Everything else was reliable online and bot play.

That became **Backgammon Reserve**: [https://apps.apple.com/us/app/backgammon-reserve/id6772647848](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/backgammon-reserve/id6772647848)

One month after release:

* 5.0 rating from 19 reviews
* 207 total users
* 61 active this week
* 17 active in the past 24 hours
* 1,099 bot games
* 344 live games
* 184 async games (24 hours per move)

Fewer users than I hoped for at this point. The bright side is that the people who found it stick around, and a smaller base has given me room to work out the kinks without doing it in front of a crowd. I think if I keep at it and ramp up marketing it could become one of the most popular backgammon apps on the store.

**The point of this post:** if you're a beginner like me, a simple evergreen game is a good way to get your feet wet on something that actually ships. The rules already exist, there's no world to build, and you can put your effort into the parts AI is genuinely good at. There's a lot of outdated evergreen games where you can see from reviews that people are hoping for something more modern and better. There's amazing stuff being made in this community, but I think the reality is that most of the ambitious ideas by beginners will stall before they're playable.

Built this entirely with Claude Code and Supabase is the backend database that supports multiplayer and tracking of stats. It took me about 3 months to get it live on the app store. Happy to answer anything about the build if it's useful.
